# Fixture repository and oracles

Status: carried over from the 2026-10-07 plan, change oracles and the sibling fixture added 2026-10-14 · the week oracle becomes `go test` in M0, still-here and change oracles in M1, web escaping in M3

`internal/fixture` builds this repository (`fixture.Main`) and the [sibling fixture](#sibling-fixture) (`fixture.Sibling`) in temporary directories for `go test`. Every number below is an oracle: a change that moves one fails CI. Each oracle exists so that one specific wrong implementation fails, and that implementation is named next to it.

CI runs real git; porcelain output is never faked. The `GitRunner` port exists so git flags live in one place, not so tests can avoid running git.

## Setup

- **Dates.** `GIT_AUTHOR_DATE` and `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE` are 12:00:00Z on the stated day. The 2026-10-06 commits use the times in the table instead, so their order is stable.
- **Window.** `--now 2026-10-07T00:00:00Z`, so the default week starts at `2026-09-30T00:00:00Z`. No commit sits on that boundary.
- **Blank lines.** Every week insertion except Frank's `spaced.py` is a non-blank line. The blank inside `service.py` was committed in January, so it is a still-here fact, not a week fact.
- **Mailmap.** The repo config sets `log.mailmap=false`. The test passes this file with `--mailmap`:

```
Ada Example <ada@example.com> <ada@other.example>
```

- **Deny list.** The deny list used in M0 includes patterns that deny `go.sum`, a `vendor` segment, and the two consecutive segments `bootstrap/cache`. `gen_out.py` is denied by the header sniff, not by a path pattern.

## Measured blame

Measured on 2026-10-08 with Git 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155). The repository for that run contained only these `app.py` and `service.py` commits, plus a work-tree `.mailmap` with the Ada line above. Sibling files in the real fixture change the commit SHAs, but not which author owns each line. `git blame -w -M -e service.py` printed:

```
^e9db5aa app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-01 12:00:00 +0000 1) def beta_stable_block():
^e9db5aa app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-01 12:00:00 +0000 2)     return "beta stable block here"
^e9db5aa app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-01 12:00:00 +0000 3) def alpha_moved_block():
^e9db5aa app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-01 12:00:00 +0000 4)
^e9db5aa app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-01 12:00:00 +0000 5)     return "alpha moved block kept"
2c7a4b6b app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-02 12:00:00 +0000 6) def gamma_added_later():
2c7a4b6b app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-02 12:00:00 +0000 7)     return "gamma added by second mail"
d720564f service.py (<bob@example.com> 2026-10-06 13:00:00 +0000 8) def delta_bob_added():
d720564f service.py (<bob@example.com> 2026-10-06 13:00:00 +0000 9)     return "delta added on the branch"
```

Gamma's author header was `ada@other.example`, and the mailmap rewrote `author-mail` to `ada@example.com` before counting. Non-blank lines in the file: Ada 6 (beta 2, alpha 2, gamma 2), Bob 2 (delta). Ada is the majority owner (`6/8 >= 0.5`); Bob is not.

`--line-porcelain` emitted four groups, of sizes 2, 3, 2 and 2:

- Beta is the first size-2 group.
- Alpha is the size-3 group. It is separate from beta even though both lines belong to the init commit, because blame starts a new group when the original line numbers are not contiguous (`4 1 2`, then `1 3 3`).
- The blank line is the middle content line of the size-3 group. Its record repeats the author headers, has no fourth field, and its content is a single tab.

The init SHA in that isolated run is `e9db5aab2e60fc152a91b4249739fcb8d0c7cfc2`:

```

author Ada Example

committer Ada Example
committer-mail <ada@example.com>
committer-time 1767268800

	    return "alpha moved block kept"
```

`--porcelain` (not `--line-porcelain`) on the same file printed the beta continuation line as `e9db5aab2e60fc152a91b4249739fcb8d0c7cfc2 5 2`, followed by the tab-prefixed content, with no second `author` line. CI runs `--line-porcelain`; the parser still accepts the suppressed form ([blame-collector.md](../../docs/spec/blame-collector.md#porcelain-parsing)).

Wrong implementations this catches:

- **Group-size multiplier.** It scores the size-3 group as 3 and the file as Ada 7 / Bob 2. The tab-line counter scores that group as 2, giving Ada 6 / Bob 2.
- **Four-field-only matcher.** It drops alpha's blank line and its `return` line.
- **Missing `-M`.** Beta goes to Bob's reorder commit and alpha stays with Ada. The file becomes Ada 4 / Bob 4, both are majority owners, and the 6/2 oracle fails. Note that dropping `-M` moves the block that moved up, which is beta.
- **Blocks too short.** The previous draft's short lines (`def alpha():`, a blank, `return 1`, `def beta():`, `return 2`) are 15 and 14 alphanumeric characters. On the same git, `-w -M` gave the same result as running without `-M`, so those lines are not the fixture.

## Week oracle (M0, `TestWeekOracle`)

`lines_added` counts numstat insertions, blank lines included, on any path that received a role. `prod_lines_added` is the `prod` subset. Assert the set of rows: the display order (`lines_added` descending, then email ascending) is not a rank.

| Who | Email | Commits | lines_added | prod_lines_added |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bob Builder | `bob@example.com` | 2 | 11 | 11 |
| Ivy Tester | `ivy@example.com` | 1 | 4 | 0 |
| Frank & Sons | `frank@example.com` | 1 | 3 | 3 |
| Ada Example | `ada@example.com` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Dana Dev | `dana@example.com` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Erin Editor | `erin@example.com` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Jules Note | `jules@example.com` | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| GitHub Copilot (bot table) | `copilot@bot.example` | 1 | 3 | 3 |

Why each row is what it is:

- **Bob, 11.** The merge's first-parent diff adds `side.py` (2) and `side_week.py` (7), which is 9. It does not add `main_only.py`, which is already on the first parent. Delta adds 2.
  - `--no-merges` drops the merge and keeps Cara's October commit, so Cara appears and Bob's 11 becomes 2.
  - `-m` alone changes nothing on 2.50.1: under `--first-parent` it still yields the first-parent diff, so Bob stays 11. Dropping `--first-parent` as well diffs the merge against its second parent too, which adds `main_only.py`'s 5 lines, so Bob becomes 16, and the walk reaches Cara's October commit, so Cara appears with 7.
- **Cara absent.** Her February commit is outside the window, and her October commit is not on the first-parent walk; its 7 lines are part of Bob's merge diff. Gina and Hank are absent too.
- **Erin, 1.** With default rename detection, her row is 1 insertion and 0 deletions on `new_name.py`. `--no-renames` would record a full-file add. Storing the raw `old_name.py => new_name.py` string would fail classification.
- **Frank, 3.** Numstat counts 3 insertions, but only 2 of his lines are non-blank. A week counter that skips blanks fails here. Frank's still-here count is 2.
- **Ivy, 4 and 0.** `tests/test_service.py` matches the segment pattern `(^|/)tests(/|$)`, but the substring `/tests/` does not occur in it. `notes.csv` is unclassified and adds 0, yet the commit still counts.
- **Jules, 0.** A commit that touches only an unclassified path still makes a row.
- **One Ada row.** Her in-window commit is authored as `ada@other.example` while `log.mailmap=false`. `%aN`/`%aE` give one row at `ada@example.com`; `%an`/`%ae` would give a second row.

## Still-here oracle (M1, `TestStillHereOracle`)

The headline counts `prod` non-blank lines only.

| Who | prod_nonblank_lines | majority_files | Bot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ada Example | 10 (`service.py` 6, `new_name.py` 3, `ada_week.py` 1) | 3 | no |
| Cara Dev | 9 (`side.py` 2, `side_week.py` 7) | 2 | no |
| Bob Builder | 7 (`service.py` 2, `main_only.py` 5) | 1 (`main_only.py` only) | no |
| Frank & Sons | 2 | 1 (`spaced.py`) | no |
| Gina Split | 2 | 1 (`split.py`) | no |
| Hank Split | 2 | 1 (`split.py`) | no |
| Dana Dev | 1 | 1 (`kept.py`) | no |
| Erin Editor | 1 | 0 (`1/4` of `new_name.py`) | no |
| GitHub Copilot | 3 | 1 (`bot.py`) | yes |

- **`split.py` is a 2/2 split.** Gina and Hank each have `majority_files == 1`, and the file counts once. A reducer that uses only `max()` fails one of those two assertions. The prefix would still be Ada and Cara, which is why the assertion is on both authors rather than on the prefix.
- **The concentration walk.**
  - `files_with_majority` is 10: `service.py`, `new_name.py`, `ada_week.py`, `kept.py`, `spaced.py`, `split.py` (counted once), `side.py`, `side_week.py`, `main_only.py`, `bot.py`.
  - The sum of `majority_files` is 11. Half of 10 is 5.0.
  - Sorted by `majority_files`, then `prod_nonblank_lines`, then email: Ada (3, 10) brings the running sum to 3; Cara (2, 9) brings it to 5; stop.
  - `authors_in_prefix` = 2, `bots_in_prefix` = 0.
- **Excluded files.** No headline lines come from `tests/test_service.py`, `go.sum`, `vendor/lib.py`, `vendor/new.py`, `gen_out.py`, `bootstrap/cache/config.php`, `notes.csv` or `extra.csv`.
  - A segment check that compares one path component to `bootstrap/cache` leaves the PHP file in `prod`, and Ada's 10 becomes 14.
  - Dropping the mailmap splits Ada's January `ada@other.example` lines into a second person, which fails her 10.

## Change oracles (M1, `TestChangeOracles`)

These values were derived by hand from the History table and the definitions in [metrics.md](../../docs/metrics.md#change-facts-shared-by-durable1-and-simplifying1), then confirmed with plain git 2.50.1: `log -p -U0 -w`, `blame -w -M --line-porcelain`, `rev-list L^1..L` and `log --grep`. The commands and their output are in the pull request for issue #3. No stillhere code produced any of them.

With `--now 2026-10-07T00:00:00Z`, every window is half-open and starts and ends at 00:00:00Z:

| Window | Interval | Main fixture landings in it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `durable@1` cohort | `[2025-10-07, 2026-07-09)` | 7, from 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-01 |
| `simplifying@1` window and `who_knows@1` recent landers | `[2026-07-09, 2026-10-07)` | 9, all on 2026-10-06 |
| `knowledge_loss@1` activity | `[2026-04-10, 2026-10-07)` | the same 9 |

Assert values, not display order. Ratios are exact fractions; three decimals are shown for reading. Short commit IDs are for debugging; tests should not assert them.

### durable@1 (main fixture)

| Who | Σ surviving / Σ added | durable@1 | N | Ranked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ada Example | 9 / 9 (rows 1, 2) | 1.000 | 2 | no, below 10 |
| Bob Builder | 5 / 7 (rows 3, 7) | 0.714 | 2 | no |
| Gina Split | 2 / 2 | 1.000 | 1 | no |
| Hank Split | 2 / 2 | 1.000 | 1 | no |

No one else has a value.

- **Bob's move (row 3).** The `-U0 -w` patch keeps alpha and gamma where they are and re-adds beta at the top: 2 added, 2 removed. Blame `-M` credits beta's two lines to the init commit, so the move keeps 0 of its 2. By definition, a move inside one file scores 0 for the mover. That is open decision 6: `durable@2` would blame at the landing commit and leave the move out of `added`. Ada's init keeps all 7 of its lines.
- **Ada's rename (row 4).** With rename detection the patch has no content lines. It adds nothing, so it is not a cluster, and Ada's N is 2, not 3.
- **Cara has no value.** Both her commits landed with row 8 on 2026-10-06, inside 90 days, although `e08df80` was written on 2026-02-01. The cohort goes by landing time.
- **Merges.** Row 8 is outside the cohort, and no line at HEAD is blamed to a merge commit.
- **Blank lines.** Row 1 adds the blank inside alpha, and it counts in neither column.

Wrong implementations this catches:

- **Missing `-M` in blame.** Beta goes to the move: Ada 7/9 (0.778), Bob 7/7.
- **`--no-renames` in the patch.** Row 4 adds the 6 non-blank lines of `service.py` and keeps none: Ada 9/15 (0.600), with N 3.
- **Numstat instead of non-blank lines.** Row 1 adds 5 lines of `app.py`: Ada 9/10.
- **Roles or the deny list ignored.** Row 1 also adds the 2 lines of `tests/test_service.py`, or the 23 denied lines.
- **No mailmap.** `ada@other.example` becomes a second person with 2/2.
- **Commit time instead of landing time.** `e08df80` joins the cohort: Cara 2/2, with N 1.
- **N counts landings.** Ada's N becomes 3.

Wrong implementations this catches:

- **Missing `-M`.** `service.py` becomes Ada 4, Bob 4, with both as majority owners.
- **`max()` only.** `split.py` loses one of its two owners.
- **No window on landers.** Gina and Hank appear as recent landers of `split.py`.
- **Crediting the merger, or patching with `log --first-parent -p`.** Bob replaces Cara as the recent lander of `side.py`: with `--first-parent`, git gives row 8 its first-parent diff, which adds `side.py` and `side_week.py` as Bob's.
- **Commit time instead of landing time.** `side.py` has no recent lander, because `e08df80` was written in February.

### AI-assisted tags and reverts (main fixture)

There are none. No commit has a `Co-authored-by` trailer, so no landing is AI-assisted: the share is 0 of 16 landings. GitHub Copilot's 2026-10-06 commit names no human co-author, so it is a bot commit, not an AI-assisted one, and it stays in the bot table. The revert query returns nothing.

## Sibling fixture

`fixture.Sibling(t)` builds a second repository, named `sibling`, for the change cases that the main History must not hold. Those are AI-assisted trailers, reverts, a reformat listed in `.git-blame-ignore-revs`, a whitespace-only change, simplifying deletions, and enough landings to rank someone. A separate repository keeps the main oracles from moving.

### Sibling setup

- **Dates.** Every commit is at 12:00:00Z on the stated day, with the same author and committer. No commit is within a day of 2025-10-07, 2026-04-10, 2026-07-09, 2026-09-07 or 2026-09-30, so no window membership depends on how a boundary is treated.
- **Now.** `--now 2026-10-07T00:00:00Z`, the same as the main fixture. The windows are the ones in the table at the top of the [change oracles](#change-oracles-m1-testchangeoracles).
- **Mailmap.** The repo config sets `log.mailmap=false`. The test passes this file with `--mailmap`. It maps the GitHub noreply address in C1's trailer to Pia:

```
Pia Pair <pia@example.com> <81234567+piapair@users.noreply.github.com>
```

- **Content.** Where a row gives only a line count, the file holds lines `<name>_<i> = <i>`, and the subject is `feat: add <file>`. Every non-blank line is unique in the repository.
- **Commit IDs.** They are stable, because the build is hermetic and uses SHA-1: HEAD is `d8d9a79387bdaa6e9da6153a9c886c1a4bcfcdfd`. Here they are part of the content, because the revert messages and `.git-blame-ignore-revs` contain full commit IDs. Tests should still find a landing by its row (date and author), not by its SHA.

| Q1 | `Co-authored-by: Claude Dupont <92345678+cdupont@users.noreply.github.com>` | no: a human co-author | | Quinn; Claude Dupont gets nothing |
| The other 37 landings | none | no | | their author |

The AI-assisted share is 4 of the 42 landings in the last 365 days.

Wrong implementations this catches:

- **A case-sensitive trailer key.** L3 is missed. A case-sensitive `git log --grep='^Co-authored-by:'` lists four commits and not L3. Git's trailer parsing, `%(trailers:key=Co-authored-by)`, finds all five.
- **Matching the name.** Q1 is tagged because its co-author is named Claude.
- **Matching `noreply` loosely.** Q1 is tagged through its GitHub noreply address.
- **Reading only the landing commit's trailers.** M is not tagged.
- **Crediting C1's author.** C1 goes to Copilot in the bot table, and Pia's `durable@1` N drops to 1.
- **Co-authors not canonicalised.** C1 goes to `81234567+piapair@users.noreply.github.com`, a second person.
- **Crediting human co-authors.** Claude Dupont appears with Q1's 6 lines.

## Tests that are not extra commits in this history

Ada's oracle stays stable only if these cases stay out of the fixture repo.

- **Classify** (`TestClassify`):
  - `tests/test_service.py` gets role `test`, and `bootstrap/cache/config.php` is denied.
  - A faked size above `max_bytes` is `too_big`; do not commit a 400 KB blob.
  - Pin the precedence among path roles with `tests/fixtures/x.py` ([classification.md](../../docs/spec/classification.md#roles)).
- **Rename paths** (`TestNumstatRename`, a small repository built with `git fast-import`): the collector reads numstat with `-z` ([week-collector.md](../../docs/spec/week-collector.md#parsing)), so each form git would print without it gives the true destination and source, in week and scan runs alike. `dir/{old => new}/file.py` gives `dir/new/file.py`; `x/{y => }/z.py` gives `x/z.py`, not `x//z.py`; `a => b => c` gives `b => c` renamed from `a`, with no warning; a modified file named `{x => y}.py` keeps its name and is not a rename; quoted and octal-escaped names keep their own bytes. Scan runs add each file's non-blank lines from its own patch, so a blank line added in a rename counts in numstat only.
- **Policy** (`TestPolicy`):
  - A user file that omits `[bots]` exits 2 and names `bots`.
  - `--days 1` against `[week].days = 7` writes `window.days` 1, `days_from` `cli`, and `since` `2026-10-06T00:00:00Z`.
  - `policy.sha256` stays the hash of the file.
- **Attributes** (`TestAttributes`, a tiny second repo):
  - A packaged deny plus `-linguist-generated` is not denied.
  - No deny plus `linguist-generated` is denied.
  - A deny with one attribute unset and the other set stays denied.
  - Repeat all three against a bare clone of that repo; without `--source` every case would read `unspecified`.
- **Loader** (`TestDenyListLoads`): a `generated_paths.txt` line that `regexp.Compile` rejects, such as a lookahead `(?=…)` (RE2 has none), fails the test. The real file's header names RE2, Linguist (MIT), and the upstream commit that was read.
- **Clone health** (`TestCloneHealth`):
  - A `--depth 1` clone warns `shallow-clone` and has no blame facts.
  - A `--filter=blob:none` clone warns `partial-clone`, and has commit facts but no line facts.
  - With a fake promisor URL, assert that nothing connects under `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`. Skip that assertion below Git 2.44, but never unset the variable.
- **Ignore-revs** (`TestIgnoreRevs`): a root `.git-blame-ignore-revs` at the scanned SHA is used and recorded; `--ignore-revs-file` on a multi-repo run exits 2.
- **Prefix with odd M** (`TestConcentrationOddM`): three authors with `majority_files` 1 each, so M = 3 and half is 1.5, with equal lines on two of them. The walk stops at ≥ 1.5, and the email tie-break decides who the second author is.
- **Display name** (`TestDisplayName`): one email, no mailmap name, two names with equal counts. The newer committer timestamp wins; equal timestamps fall through to UTF-8 bytes ascending.
- **Cache** (`TestCacheAmend`, only if open decision #3 is approved): blame the fixture, then amend a blamed commit away without `git gc`. `git cat-file -e` of the old HEAD still exits 0, and the next scan misses every blame fact.
- **Hotspots** (only with open decision #1):
  - Option A: with the jar absent, `hotspots.status = skipped`, `reason = jar-not-found`, and still-here rows are unchanged. CSV fixtures under `testdata/maat_csv/` cover an ambiguous display name and a path that no longer exists, with `ownership` as a 0–1 ratio and `degree` as an integer percent.
  - Option B: the tables equal a one-time code-maat run on this fixture.

## Discovery fixture (`TestDiscover`)

Two clones whose `origin` is `https://user:TOKENVALUE@github.com/example/widget.git`, plus a third clone with a different remote:

- The run keeps one widget and skips the other with `duplicate-repo`. The warning names the two local paths and `https://github.com/example/widget.git`, and nothing else.
- `TOKENVALUE` appears nowhere in stdout, stderr, the JSON output, or (from M1) the facts store.
- A bare repository given as `PATH`, and a bare child of a group, are scanned rather than skipped; their branch comes from `symbolic-ref HEAD`.
- A work-tree clone and a bare mirror with the same HTTPS remote are duplicates.
- `git@github.com:o/r.git` and `https://github.com/o/r.git` stay two separate repos.

## What fails CI

- **Oracles.** Any week or still-here oracle above changes. That includes Frank's 3 versus 2, Ivy's `prod_lines_added` 0, Jules's 0-line commit, Erin's rename insertion of 1, Ada's single mailmapped week row, and both Gina and Hank at `majority_files` 1.
- **Change oracles.** Any value in the change-oracle tables of either fixture changes. That includes Bob's move keeping 0 of 2, Ada's `durable@1` N of 2, Cara's absence from `durable@1`, `knowledge_loss@1` at 4/34, Lena eligible at exactly 10 clusters in both metrics, Omar not eligible at 9, S1 simplifying at exactly −20, S2 not simplifying at −16, Q1 untagged, and M tagged through P2.
- **Classification.** `tests/test_service.py` is classified `prod`, or `bootstrap/cache/config.php` is blamed.
- **Discovery.** A duplicate remote is not skipped, a scrubbed URL contains userinfo, a bare repo is skipped, or the SSH and HTTPS forms of one path are collapsed.
- **Isolation.** A repo whose git directory was removed makes a sibling repo disappear, or the run exits 1 when the sibling succeeded.
- **Policy.** The policy hash is missing from the output, a user policy missing `[bots]` exits 0, or `--days 1` leaves `window.days` at 7.
- **Draft JSON.** The output omits `errors.blame` or `group_rollups` (until M1 supersedes the format).
- **Cache**, only if open decision #3 ships: a blame-cache miss on the second scan of the untouched fixture, or a hit after an amend without `gc`.
- **M3 web** (`TestWebEscaping`): a rendered page contains an email address, or the unescaped bytes `Frank & Sons`. The escaped text node `Frank &amp; Sons` is required. Pages are rendered with Go `html/template`. The 2026-10-07 rule against any `<script` element belonged to the single-file HTML design and is superseded.
- **Java** is never required in CI.

Work out the expected values from the history above and write them into this file before writing the code that computes them. The implementation must never produce its own oracle.

- **Done for M1 (issue #3):** `durable@1` per landing and per person, `simplifying@1`, revert detection, AI-assisted tagging, `knowledge_loss@1` and `who_knows@1`. They are in [Change oracles](#change-oracles-m1-testchangeoracles) and the [Sibling fixture](#sibling-fixture), which holds the revert and AI-assisted cases so that the main oracles don't move.
- **GitHub sync contract tests**: recorded API responses (pull requests, reviews, review comments, team membership, the viewer's verified emails) under `testdata/github/`, with no live calls in CI. Derive the expected facts by hand.
